title: Existence of a quasi-kernel (Chvátal–Lovász)
statement: (Chvátal and Lovász, 1974.) Let $D$ be a loopless digraph on a finite vertex set $V$; that is, no vertex has an arc to itself. Then $D$ admits an independent set $S \subseteq V$ — no two distinct vertices of $S$ are joined by an arc of $D$ in either direction — such that every vertex $v \notin S$ is reachable from some vertex $u \in S$ by a directed path of length one or two: either $u \to v$ is an arc of $D$, or there is a vertex $w$ with arcs $u \to w$ and $w \to v$.
